metadata.description: A human identity/account — an ACTOR that DCM authenticates and authorizes (the RBAC bridge — `Grouping` subject_bindings plus the function-capability matrix). Fills the named-but-unbuilt Identity.* slot (naming-conventions §2; resource-type-hierarchy §Identity). Holds NO secret material — credentials are referenced (Security.CredentialRef). Backs the built-in auth provider's local users and, when federated, references the external IdP subject (PIP). Its actor_type is `human`, from the one closed actor-type vocabulary (universal-audit).

handle.description: Login handle / username, unique within the implementation.

display_name.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Identity.Person spec.

email.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Identity.Person spec.

actor_type.description: From the closed actor-type vocabulary (universal-audit); a Person is always `human`.

authenticated_by.description: handle/uuid of the Auth Provider (auth capability) or Security.DirectoryService that authenticates this person. Default: the built-in provider (no external IdP required).

credential_ref.description: Reference to Security.CredentialRef — the credential record for this person. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

external_subject.description: The external IdP subject id when federated (a PIP reference, resolved not stored).

status.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Identity.Person spec.

actor_uuid.description: The stable actor id referenced by role-assignments and by grouping (access_grouping) membership.

relationships.description: Member of an access grouping (access_grouping) or Identity.Group; membership drives role binding (the RBAC bridge — `Grouping` subject_bindings plus the function-capability matrix).

context.purpose: Models a human account — the actor that gets authenticated, authorized, and audited.
context.plain_description: One human's identity: its `handle` (the login name) and its `actor_type` — always `human`, and required alongside the handle — plus display name, email, status, and how they authenticate (the built-in provider by default, or a directory/IdP when federated). It carries no secret material — a password or key is referenced through a Security.CredentialRef, never stored. Every audited action and role assignment points back at this record's stable actor id.
use_when: You need human accounts as records that role assignments and audit trails reference.
You need a federated user tied to their external IdP subject without copying the IdP's data.
not_for: Automation, agents, or API-key holders — Identity.ServiceAccount.
The credential itself — Security.CredentialRef; a person references credentials, never contains them.
The directory server — Security.DirectoryService is the server; this is one identity in it.
works_with: Identity.Group — memberships that drive role binding.
Security.CredentialRef — the person's credentials, by reference.
Security.DirectoryService — the external authenticator when federated.
